subject: Media Literacy
title: Evaluating Expert Sources
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Evaluating Expert Sources.

hook.text: A 'Harvard doctor' quoted in a health article turns out to be a dentist commenting outside his field.

buildup.text: News stories quote experts to add credibility. But not all experts are equally qualified on every topic.

discovery.text: Check an expert's specific field, published research, institutional affiliation, and potential conflicts of interest.

twist.text: Media often uses the same few experts repeatedly because they give good quotes, not because they're the most qualified.

climax.text: A real expert speaks cautiously within their field. A media expert speaks confidently about everything.

punchline.text: An expert in one field is a layperson in another. Check the match.

quiz.question: How should you evaluate an expert quoted in news?
options: Check their specific field, research, affiliation, and potential conflicts
Experts are always right in any field
